subject: Private stack onboarding: platform-fee alignment & grandfathering ask
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cascadehealth.com>, procurement@cascadehealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private stack onboarding: platform-fee alignment & grandfathering ask

Hi Alex / Cascade procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday — appreciate the detailed run-through of your migration timeline and the regulatory constraints you shared. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a concrete commercial option on the table that addresses two signals you mentioned: predictability of unit economics during the migration window, and minimizing up-front platform fee impact for an organization moving from hosted to Private (VPC).

High-level proposal (summary):
- Platform fee: keep the standard Private platform fee but grandfather a 50% reduced platform fee for the first 6 months post-cutover (applies to invoice months 1-6).
- Support: map your current hosted response SLAs to our Bronze -> Silver mapping; include 24/7 incident escalation during onboarding (first 90 days) at no incremental charge.
- Consumption fallback: if actual consumption in months 4–6 is >120% of forecast, we offer an automatic consumption-based rebate (credits applied to month 8) to avoid unexpected overage surprises.

I've attached a draft SOW that reflects the implementation milestones and a pricing matrix with scenarios based on node counts and expected token throughput. If this looks directionally okay, we'd like to: 1) lock the commercial model in writing, 2) get a technical kickoff date, and 3) share a DocuSign for signature.

Open questions from our side where your input would be helpful:
- Do you need guaranteed node affinity for any regulated workloads (we can reserve nodes in a region as part of Dedicated on demand)?
- Are you comfortable with the proposed 6-month grandfathering window, or is your preference a calendar-year amortization?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the SOW line-by-line.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Cascade_SOW_v2.pdf (PDF, 312 KB)]
[Attachment: pricing_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 48 KB)]

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cascadehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private stack onboarding: platform-fee alignment & grandfathering ask

Naomi — thanks for the fast follow. A few thoughts from procurement and finance: we like the spirit of the grandfathering approach, but the 50% residual platform fee in months 1–6 is still above what our CFO is comfortable with given our hosted-to-private credit we hold from our previous vendor. Two alternatives we'd like you to consider: 

A) 90% reduction on the platform fee for months 1–3, then revert to 60% reduction months 4–6 (shorter runway, deeper early discount); OR
B) Keep your 50% for months 1–6 but include a right-to-audit clause and a one-time migratory credit equal to 2 months of platform fee applied after go-live.

Also — the consumption fallback is great; can you confirm that the measurement will use our token reports (we'll share the CloudWatch-style export)? And we'll need the SOW to reflect a 30-day termination-with-cause carveout tied to unresolved P1 incidents during the first 180 days.

Appreciate it,
Alex Rivera
Director, Procurement — Cascade Health
[procurement@cascadehealth.com]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Private stack onboarding: platform-fee alignment & grandfathering ask

Team — forwarding Cascade's response. They pushed back on the 50% plateau; procurement proposed either deeper early discount or the 2-month migratory credit. They also want explicit measurement requirements for the consumption fallback and a termination-with-cause clause tied to P1s in first 180 days.

Quick suggested concession matrix (my callouts):
- Option A (short, deep): 90% platform fee discount months 1–3, 60% months 4–6 — margin impact is higher short term; good for faster acceptance.
- Option B (credit): keep original 50% months 1–6 + one-time migratory credit equal to 2 months of platform fee — more predictable revenue recognition, less immediate margin hit.
- Measurement: accept Cascade's token CSV export as the primary dataset; we add a max 7-day reconciliation window for disputes.
- Termination-with-cause: accept 30-day remediation window for P1; require formal SRE escalation steps before termination path is available.

Notes: their deal size is decent (projected ARR if they convert ~ $1.1M). If we go Option A we should ask for a 12–18 month commit on node minimums; if Option B, we can be more flexible. Please weigh in with a clear preference — I want to get a single counter back to them by EOD PST.

Thanks,
Naomi

[Inline: pricing_matrix.xlsx referenced above]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private stack onboarding: platform-fee alignment & grandfathering ask

Naomi — I prefer Option B (migratory credit). Rationale: preserves our headline platform fee, better revenue predictability, and keeps margins relatively intact vs deep up-front discounting. We can approve a 2-month migratory credit capped at the invoiced platform fee for months 1–2.

We should also: 
- Include the audit/reporting acceptance language: their token CSV (UTC timestamps, token counts, consumer id) accepted as primary, with us reserving right to request a weekly aggregated extract for the first 3 months.
- For P1 termination: accept 30-day remediation but require an SRE runbook and a technical onboarding checklist (in SOW) as a gating item. If they don't complete gating items within 45 days of cutover, standard termination steps apply.

David — please confirm the impact on revenue recognition and whether legal needs to review any special audit language. If legal is fine, Naomi — go ahead and send this counter (Option B + measurement + SOW gate language).

—Marissa
VP, Commercials, Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@cascadehealth.com>, procurement@cascadehealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-07-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private stack onboarding: platform-fee alignment & grandfathering ask

Alex — thank you and appreciate the clear options. We discussed internally and can proceed with this counter if you are aligned: 

Our counter (final):
- Platform fee: 50% reduction applied months 1–6 (as originally proposed).
- Migratory credit: one-time credit equal to 2 months of platform fee applied after go-live (credit capped at the invoiced platform fee for months 1–2). This credit is treated as a post-go-live invoice credit (impacting month 2 or 3 invoice depending on reconciliation).
- Measurement: we accept your token CSV export (UTC timestamps + token counts + consumer_id). Redwood will provide a reconciliation report within 7 business days of month close. Disputes can be raised within 14 days and will be adjudicated by joint SRE owners.
- P1 termination: 30-day remediation window with required SRE runbook and an onboarding checklist included as SOW gating items. Failure to complete gating items within 45 days after cutover will allow standard contract remediation steps.

Next steps: I've attached an updated SOW that includes the gating checklist and the audit/reporting appendix. If this is acceptable, please confirm and I will share the DocuSign link for signature.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
[Attachment: Cascade_SOW_v2.pdf (PDF, 318 KB)]
[Link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/CASCADE-ONPREM-2026]
